western.temperament: Expressive, quick-witted, curious, intelligent, adaptable. Shadow: scattered, fickle, two-faced, nervous, inconsistent; moods swing between free and restless. Symbol: the twins Castor and Pollux, one mortal and one divine; when Castor died, Pollux asked Zeus to share his immortality and the two were united in the sky.

chinese.temperament: Diligent, compassionate, generous, calm under pressure, responsible, tolerant and trustworthy. Shadow: trusting to the point of being fooled, rarely asks for help, impatient, not good at managing money. The pig symbolizes wealth, honesty and plenty (piggy banks).
chinese.clash: Snake (Wikipedia also lists Monkey as a harm pair and Pig with itself as self-punishment)

symbolism.meaning: The name comes from Nahuatl tlahcomiztli, from tlahco- 'half, middle' + miztli 'cougar', so 'half-puma' or 'half-cat'. Miztli itself is attested in Sahagun and Molina's 1571 dictionary. A name that sizes the animal as half of a big cat is the one genuine cultural hook.

Chilango, citing UNAM experts, says the cacomixtle does not appear in prehispanic mythology, though people lived alongside it. Treat this honestly: there is no myth to borrow. The page should not invent one.

Castor and Pollux: Pollux asked Zeus to share his immortality with his dead twin, and the two were united in the heavens. Pairs well with an animal whose life runs on calls traded with a neighbor it rarely meets.
人怕出名猪怕壮 rén pà chū míng zhū pà zhuàng: people fear fame the way pigs fear fattening up for slaughter; fame has its price. Already on the live page (in traditional characters 豬 zhū, 壯 zhuàng).

symbolism.culture: Other species, do not use here
symbolism.meaning: 'Miner's cat' (settlers kept ringtails as mousers), Spanish 'nimble thief' gloss, and the Mexico City urban cacomixtles seen in all 16 boroughs all refer to Bassariscus astutus, the ringtail, which is a separate Zodi Animal (Taurus x Monkey, slug ringtail). ADW gives the 'nimble thief' meaning without a source.
Any 'cacomistle spirit animal' or totem meaning: none found with a traditional source.

fusion.temperament: Our reading: mutable Air (Gemini) over yin Water (Pig). Gemini talks, the Pig forages alone and does not perform. The Cacomistle is the voice in the canopy: solitary, high, unseen, and calling to its neighbors for hours. Mercury gives the calls; the Pig gives the patient night of feeding on figs. Air sits outside the five phases, so the Pig's Water is the only true element; Gemini colors it without changing it.
fusion.gifts: Our reading: long-distance closeness (the hours-long call); range without fuss; generosity and trust from the Pig; quick reading of a situation from above; comfort being half of two things (half-puma, raccoon kin, twin).
fusion.shadow: Our reading: Gemini's inconsistency plus the Pig's reluctance to ask for help. Talking instead of landing; staying a rumor; letting a neighbor know your voice but never your face. The fattened-pig proverb used as an excuse never to be seen.
fusion.love: Our reading: loves by keeping in touch, daily, across distance; a long-distance relationship is less scary to it than a shared floor. Twin logic: once committed, will share its best with the partner the way Pollux shared his sky.
fusion.money: Our reading: the Pig's luck with plenty and weak money management, plus Gemini's many side interests. Earns from several branches at once; needs one dull, fixed account it does not touch.
fusion.conflict: Our reading: moves rather than fights; changes branches, keeps talking, avoids the face-to-face. Territories do not overlap, so it keeps clear borders and defends them by voice, not claws. Helpful habit: agree on one fixed place to settle things.

candidate_lines: Your voice crosses a hundred hectares of night forest before your face ever shows up, and the neighbor who answers knows you better than anyone who has actually seen you.
The Nahuatl speakers called you half a puma. You have spent years quietly correcting the fraction, but only to whoever is close enough to hear it.
Give you a fruiting fig high in the canopy and one good neighbor calling back across the dark, and the crowd on the forest floor can carry on without you.
Pollux split his sky with his twin and never asked for it back. When you love someone you split yours the same way, and you rarely mention what it cost.
People fear fame, pigs fear fattening. You worked that out long before anyone said it to you, and you keep your best work one branch above the count.
The ringed tail that flashes in a torch beam is doing the balancing. What people call your showy side is the part keeping you on the branch.

fact_audit.note: 狸 lí means fox, raccoon dog, or fox-like animal (also used in 狸猫 for wild cats). The cacomistle is a raccoon relative: Chinese Wikipedia calls it 中美蓬尾浣熊 zhōngměi péngwěi huànxióng. Use 浣熊 huànxióng (raccoon family) or the full name, with pinyin.

fact_audit.fact: IUCN classifies it Least Concern, 'locally common across the northern part of its range', yet field surveys routinely record it as one of the least-detected mammals present.
fact_audit.note: Least Concern is correct (ADW, Wikipedia). The 'locally common' quote could not be checked (IUCN page would not load) and is contradicted: ADW says it is nowhere common in its range; Wikipedia says it is generally an uncommon sight. The survey claim cites a PMC paper (Ecology and Evolution, 2025) that was behind a captcha; not verified. The page's whole archetype ('common but unconfirmed') rests on this; rewrite as 'listed Least Concern, but rarely seen'.

fact_audit.fact: Nocturnal and highly arboreal, almost never comes to the ground, canopy from sea level to 2,000 m.
fact_audit.note: ADW, near verbatim: 'almost never comes down to the ground', sea level to 2000 m. Wikipedia: middle and upper canopy.

fact_audit.fact: Climbers in its genus can rotate the hind foot nearly 180 degrees to descend headfirst.
fact_audit.verdict: UNVERIFIABLE for this species (borrowed from ringtail)
fact_audit.note: ADW documents 180-degree hindfoot rotation for Bassariscus astutus, the ringtail. Neither ADW nor Wikipedia says it for B. sumichrasti. The page hedges with 'in its genus', but it then reads the trait as the cacomistle's. The ringtail is a separate Zodi Animal; this fact belongs on its page.

fact_audit.fact: Name from Nahuatl tlacomiztli, roughly 'half mountain lion'; raccoon family, no closer relation to cats.
fact_audit.note: Dictionary.com: tlahcomiztli, tlahco- half + miztli cougar. Online Nahuatl Dictionary gives tla'comiztli 'semi-puma'. Use tlahcomiztli. Raccoon family is correct.

fact_audit.fact: Tail 390 to 530 mm, nearly as long as the 380 to 470 mm body; works as counterweight and balance.
fact_audit.note: Measurements match ADW and Wikipedia. Note the tail is as long as or longer than the body, so 'nearly as long' undersells it. No source found stating the counterweight function for this species.

fact_audit.fact: Solitary outside mating season; territories can run past 130 hectares; exchange loud calls with neighbors, sometimes for hours, believed to mark territory edges.
fact_audit.note: ADW: solitary except mating season; territories up to 136 ha and do not overlap; loud calls exchanged between individuals, sometimes for hours. Wikipedia gives home range of at least 20 ha, so 136 is the upper end: say 'up to about 136'. 'Believed to mark the edges' is not in ADW; label as our reading or cut.

fact_audit.fact: Purple Star block: Zi Wei Dou Shu 'maps the Cacomistle you are becoming'.
fact_audit.note: ZWDS is cast from lunar birth date and hour and contains no Zodi Animals. Reword as a plain link.

page_bugs: Name collision: Dictionary.com's first sense of 'cacomistle' is Bassariscus astutus, the ringtail, and Wikipedia notes the name is used for both. The GRID has both Ringtail (Taurus x Monkey) and Cacomistle (Gemini x Pig). The page should say plainly it means B. sumichrasti, the Central American cacomistle, and keep ringtail facts (foot rotation, miner's cat, Mexico City sightings) on the ringtail page.
Match I and II reasons say 'Your Water feeds their Wood: you are the warmth in it'. Warmth is the Wood-to-Fire image; Water feeding Wood should read as rain or roots.
Page lists ADW Bassariscus astutus as a source on the cacomistle page: that is where the borrowed foot-rotation fact came from.
Lines are set in 'a room' ('the moment a room starts taking attendance'); brief wants lines inside the canopy.
No January/February lunar new year note: correct for Gemini.
